caption: Figure 1. An example of an RGB-D object identification scene. Columns on the right show example segments, identified as positive (far right) and negative (center).
Figure 2. An example semantic analysis for a sentence from our dataset.

Figure3. Example scenes presented on Mechanical Turk. Left: A scene that elicited the descriptions "here are some red things" and "these are various types of red colored objects", both labeled as λx.color(x, red). Right: A scene associated with sentence/meaning pairs such as "this toy is orange cube" and λx.color(x, orange) ∧ shape(x, cube).
Figure 4. A summary of precision, recall, and F1 for ablated models and the joint learning model.

Figure5. Feature weights for hypothesized lexemes pairing natural language words (rows) with newly created terms referring to novel classifiers (columns), as well as the special null token. Each weight serves as an unnormalized indicator of which associations are preferred.
